title: Section · Axes grid (multi-axis from→to)
description: Multi-axis matrix of scaling dimensions. Up to 6 axes (cards with auto-hide for empty slots). Each axis: numbered eyebrow + label, a full-width tick track (7 ticks with opacity ramp suggesting growth), from→to range labels in mono, and a short body paragraph. 3-col grid → 2-col at ≤980 → 1-col at ≤640. Used for 'how the platform scales along these axes' sections after StagesList.

source.decision: PM lock 2026-05-24 — axes-grid adopted as canonical scalability pattern

gradient.recommended: subtle neutral/accent gradient only; do not use freeform decorative orbs

notes: Background is decorative and must not replace content media slots or block copy.
Preview in any supported harness with ?bg=gradient or ?bg=image&bgImage=<encoded-url>.

params.default: Service businesses scale from a single office to multiple branches and eventually multi-region operations. ServiceWand supports each shape — one team, several territories, or many regions with separate data residency.
Crews grow from a couple of techs into territory-level workforce. Scheduling, dispatch, mobile workflows, and reporting all need to keep working at every count without a tool swap.

Customer models evolve from individual one-off jobs to recurring contracts, multi-property accounts, and tiered service agreements. The customer model supports all of those without redesigning the data.
Billing starts simple (invoice when the job is done) and gets richer as operations grow: recurring contracts, partial payments, multi-currency, accounting integrations, and audit trails.
Reporting starts as a Friday spreadsheet and ends as live operational dashboards across routes, crews, billing, customer satisfaction, and asset performance — drillable to the underlying work order.

Most operations start standalone and gradually connect into the rest of the business: accounting, CRM, mapping, payments, communications. ServiceWand connects through APIs, webhooks, and configurable workflows.

notes: 6 axes by default. Empty axis labels auto-hide via :has(.axis-label:empty), so admins can ship 3 or 4 axes without editing markup.
Each axis has a 7-tick track with opacity ramp (0.15 → 1.00) — visually suggests 'growth along this axis' without claiming a specific measurement.
from → to is mono-typed so it reads as a spec, not a sentence.
